messages.subject: suggestions for plotting this data
parts:
What do you think is an effective presentation of the information in this data.
I have a drug and I want to visually compare the differences in effects between
men and women. I also have confidence intervals for the effects.

Two ways I have seen is to have each Drug in its own box and have a
line connecting
the effects. The graph would then have several of these boxes.

Or, it could look similar to what I have seen called a forest plot.
However, there
are two effects that need to be side by side. The CIs can overlap so it seems
they could not be exactly side by side.

Any suggestions? Here is some data. Thanks, Juliet

myData <- read.table(textConnection("Drug Effect_M UCI_M LCI_M
Effect_F UCI_F LCI_F
A 10 12 9 5 6 4
B 2 3 1 -2 -1 -3
C 0 1 -1 0.1 1.1 -0.9
D -5 -4 -6 3 4 2"))
closeAllConnections()

messages.author: cb25d91fd630a4e5
messages.subject: Re: suggestions for plotting this data
parts:
I wouldn't use lines, since both your variables are categorical. I
also wouldn't recommend bars, as I've come across arguments that they
are less visually succinct (and possibly misleading) than points. With
a 2x2 design, just plot one IV on the x axis and vary the color &
shape of the points by the other IV.

With respect to error bars, humans (even knowledgeable researchers)
aren't very good at interpreting error bars that represent confidence
intervals. I prefer to use Fisher's Least Significant Difference as
the error bar, that way any points whose bars fail to overlap are
significantly different (but only if the plotted effect is significant
in the omnibus anova). The code below calculates the LSD bar of the
highest order interaction in a given aov object. To use it as a bar,
plot half the LSD on each side of each data point (ex.
p+error_bar(aes(ymin=y+this_lsd/2,ymax=y-this_lsd/2)) ).

CI <- function(N, MSE, MSEdf) {Tcrit<-qt(0.975,MSEdf); Tcrit * sqrt(MSE/N)}
LSD <- function(from.aov) {
MSEdf=from.aov[length(from.aov)][[1]]$df.residual
MSE=sum(from.aov[length(from.aov)][[1]]$residuals^2)/MSEdf
N=summary(from.aov[[2]])[[1]]$Df+1
sqrt(2) * CI(N,MSE,MSEdf)

}

messages.author: 166e40180306ffff
messages.subject: Re: suggestions for plotting this data
parts:
That's a nice method. However, the funcion you provided produces the
following error:

Error in summary(from.aov[[2]])[[1]]$Df :
$ operator is invalid for atomic vectors

The MSEdf could be easier calculated by
MSEdf=df.residual(from.aov)

MSE could be easier extracted by
MSE<-deviance(from.aov)/MSEdf

N could be extracted by
x=length(resid(x))
(if it is the N of the whole model and not from the different groups,
that you need here.
Correct me, if I'm wrong)

Regards,

Erich
